scenes.narration: A method is a function that lives inside a class. It can read and change the attributes of its object through self. Some methods return an answer. Others just change the object, and return nothing. A bank account is a good example. Deposit adds to the balance. Withdraw takes from it. Think of buttons on a vending machine. Each button changes the machine's own insides. To call a method, always use brackets, even with no arguments.

code.source:
class Account:
    def __init__(self, owner, balance=0):
        self.owner = owner
        self.balance = balance

    def deposit(self, amount):
        self.balance = self.balance + amount

    def withdraw(self, amount):
        if amount > self.balance:
            return False
        self.balance = self.balance - amount
        return True

acc = Account("Asha", 100)
acc.deposit(50)
print(acc.balance)
print(acc.withdraw(500))
print(acc.withdraw(30))
print(acc.balance)

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: calling a method without brackets
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the Python error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. We wrote acc dot show, with no brackets. Python does not run the method. It prints the method itself, a bound method, with a memory address. No error, and no answer. Add the brackets, and the method runs, and returns the balance.

props.why: Without brackets you get the method object itself, not the result of running it. Brackets are what call it.

shorts.title: Return a value
shorts.hook: "Methods can return answers, just like functions."
shorts.script: Methods can return answers, just like functions. A temperature object can return its value in Fahrenheit. A withdraw method can return True when it worked, and False when it failed. The caller decides what to do with the answer. Say it out loud once. Then you remember it. Then run it, and compare with what you predicted. Try it in your own file and watch what happens. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Methods can return values.

shorts.title: No brackets
shorts.script: A tricky one. You write acc dot show, without brackets. Python prints bound method show of account object, and an address. It did not run the method. It showed it. Add the brackets, and the method actually runs. Then run it, and compare with what you predicted. Try it in your own file and watch what happens. Pause the video and type it out yourself. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
